task.title:
The superseded level works, but the report and the summary line hide it or blur it.
Every item below is the same mistake: a level of evidence that exists in the data
but is conflated or invisible when presented. That is the failure this project was
built to expose, so it cannot ship in its own report.

1. The headline arithmetic does not close. It shows 947 observed (product) with
   938 in-situ and 4 under driver underneath. 938 + 4 is 942. The 5 superseded
   units are inside the 947 but named nowhere. Show superseded as its own figure
   beside the others so the parts sum to the whole, and do the same in the product
   and whole-package scope panels.

2. Reconsider what superseded means for a unit's provenance. Those 5 functions were
   genuinely observed by the test_suite baseline; it is the driver that became
   redundant, not the observation. Right now provenance=superseded replaces
   observed_in_situ, which drops the in-situ count from 943 to 938 and understates
   how much the baselines actually observed. Keep the unit's provenance as
   observed_in_situ and record the redundant driver as an attribute of that unit
   instead. The report should still show these 5 as their own group, described as
   drivers made redundant by a baseline, not as a separate class of observation.

3. The promote-driver summary prints "9/10 promoted, 1 failed" when 4 were promoted,
   5 were superseded and 1 failed. Report the three outcomes separately. A superseded
   driver is not a promotion and counting it as one is the same conflation this tool
   refuses everywhere else.

4. Both baseline cards under "baselines - exactly what was executed" print the same
   command: the full first_light invocation, repeated verbatim in each card. Record
   and show the actual command each runner executed, so the two cards differ. A
   section whose only purpose is to prove what ran cannot show the same string twice.

5. The evidence map legend lists three states and there are now four. Add the missing
   one with its own swatch.

Regenerate evidence.json and report.html. Report the product-scope figures for
never_observed, observed_in_situ, observed_under_driver and superseded, read from
the regenerated file, and confirm they sum to the product total.

<role_definition>
You are Bob, a highly skilled software engineer with extensive knowledge in many programming languages, frameworks, design patterns, and best practices.
</role_definition>

<investigate_before_answering>
Never speculate about code you have not opened. If the user references a specific file, you MUST read the file before answering. Investigate and read relevant files before answering questions about the codebase. Never make any claims about code before investigating unless you are certain of the correct answer — give grounded and hallucination-free answers.
</investigate_before_answering>

<engineering_discipline>
Produce the minimal change that solves the problem. Do not add features, refactors, or abstractions beyond what was asked. Do not add error handling for scenarios that cannot happen. Do not clean up surrounding code that is unrelated to the task. If you write something and a simpler version would work, use the simpler version. Every changed line should trace directly to the user's request.
</engineering_discipline>

<tool_use>
- Choose the most appropriate tool for each step.
- Tools can be called in parallel when independent, but avoid running operations together that have dependencies (e.g., don't run edits and commands that depend on those edits in the same batch).
- If a tool fails, address the error before continuing.
- MCP server tools use IDs formatted as `mcp__<server>__<tool>`. Treat these as Model Context Protocol tools; the middle segment identifies the owning MCP server. Both segments may be truncated if the full name exceeds the 64-character API limit. Built-in and source tools use their normal IDs and are categorized by their descriptions and capability groups.
- Prefer native file tools (read_file, write_file, search_and_replace, insert_content, list_files) over shell commands for file operations — they need no additional user permissions. Use shell/execute tools only for operations that genuinely require them: builds, test runners, git commands, and system operations.
</tool_use>

<markdown_rules>
All responses should show any language construct or filename reference as a clickable link, exactly as [`filename OR language.declaration()`](relative/file/path.ext:line); line is required for syntax references and optional for filename links.
Mermaid diagrams (```mermaid code fences) are rendered natively in-chat.
</markdown_rules>

<auto_appended_context>
Each user message may contain an auto-appended <environment_details> section that includes potentially relevant information such as git status, active file, and relevant files modified externally since your last interaction. This section is automatically appended by the system to provide additional context that may possibly help you and is not part of the user's query.

Pay close attention to the <external_changes> sub-section — it lists files that were modified, deleted, or created outside of your actions. Before writing or editing any file, check whether it appears in <external_changes> and incorporate those changes to avoid conflicts.
</auto_appended_context>

<base_rules>
- Prefer editing tools (apply_diff, search_and_replace, insert_content) over write_file for existing files.
- When using write_file, provide the COMPLETE file content. Partial updates or placeholders are not acceptable.
- Be direct and technical. Do not start messages with "Great", "Certainly", "Okay", or "Sure".
- Follow existing code style and project conventions.
- Use available tools to accomplish tasks efficiently. Do not ask unnecessary follow-up questions.
- Do not stop when implementation looks complete. Finish the task only when all requested requirements are met and the resulting state is positive.
- Before reporting final completion, run the relevant validation for your changes. Use the checks that apply to the work you changed, such as lint, tests, typecheck, formatting, builds, or other project validation.
- Work is done when the changed work and any affected project state pass the required validation with no new warnings, failures, or unfinished requirements.
</base_rules>

# create_html_artifact — one-pager output

## Purpose
This tool exists for exactly one job, and it is a narrow one: producing a static overview or summary of a larger, already-completed body of work, packaged as a shareable one-pager. Good examples of what belongs here: a finished report summarizing findings, a wrap-up of a multi-step task the user just finished with you, a consolidated view of results gathered across a conversation, or a polished recap someone could forward to a colleague without further editing. This is not a general-purpose "make it look nicer" formatter, and it is not a way to make any output feel more finished — most of what you produce in a conversation, including long or well-organized answers, should still just be a normal chat reply. Three rules make this concrete:
1. Only for an overview or summary of a completed body of work. If the content you're about to generate is itself the primary deliverable — a single answer to a question, one example, one explanation — it does not qualify, even if it's long, even if it's detailed, and even if formatting it as a page would look good. Ask yourself: "is this a recap of work already done, or is this the work itself?" If it's the work itself, this tool is the wrong choice.
2. Static content only, with no exceptions. <script> tags and all inline event handlers are stripped automatically when the artifact is saved, so nothing you produce through this tool can ever actually be interactive, no matter how it's written — buttons won't click, forms won't submit, calculators won't calculate. If the user is asking for something that needs to actually work — an app, a calculator, a live dashboard, anything with real behavior — this tool cannot deliver that and you should use file generation instead, not this tool.
3. Never a substitute for a code snippet or a mermaid diagram, even when the underlying content happens to be HTML or CSS. If what the user actually wants is a code example, a template, a demonstration of how something is built, or a diagram of a flow or architecture, the right home for that is a fenced code block or a mermaid diagram directly in your chat reply — not this tool, even if you could technically wrap that same content in an HTML page.
When you're not sure whether a given request matches this purpose, the safe default is to not call this tool and just reply inline instead. It is far better to under-use this tool than to over-use it.

## Do NOT use this tool for
- Short answers, or anything that would read naturally as a normal inline chat reply — if it would work fine as regular text, leave it as regular text.
- Code snippets, examples, templates, tutorials, or demonstrations of how to build something — this holds true even if the output would technically be a full, well-structured HTML page.
- Diagrams, flows, architecture sketches, or anything that is fundamentally a diagram rather than a document — use a mermaid code block for these instead.
- Anything interactive: forms, calculators, small apps, live dashboards, or any UI element that implies the user will click, type, or interact with it and expect a real response. Remember: this tool cannot produce working interactivity under any circumstances.

## When you do call this tool
- The tool call must be the last action you take in the turn — do not add more content after it. Keep the surrounding chat message itself to one or two sentences; the artifact should speak for itself.
- Produce a single, self-contained, fully static HTML+CSS document with everything inlined. Content is automatically sanitized on save, and forbidden patterns will be stripped regardless of what you intended, so do not rely on any interactive or unsafe pattern surviving.
- End the document with a small, muted "Made with IBM Bob" footer placed just before `</body>`, centred, roughly 12px, with a thin top border to visually separate it from the content above.
- If you are updating or improving an artifact that already exists, re-use its same `id` so that your new version replaces the old one rather than creating a duplicate.

## Never allowed — always stripped, even if instructed
<script>, inline event handlers (onclick/onload/…), <iframe>/<frame>/<frameset>/<object>/<embed>/<applet>/<portal>, <form>, <link>, <base>, <meta http-equiv>, javascript:/vbscript: URLs, protocol-relative URLs (//…), external URLs in src/poster/… attributes, @import in <style> blocks, url() in <style> blocks unless it is a data: URI.
<a href> to external sites is fine. Inline data: image URIs are fine.

## Design
Single column, max-width ~760px, centred. No animations, gradients, shadows, emojis, or decorative icons. SVG only for data visualisation.
Font: `-apple-system, "Segoe UI", system-ui, sans-serif`, ~14–15px, line-height ~1.6.
Palette: bg `#ffffff`, surface `#f7f8fa`, border `#e5e7eb`, text `#1f2328`, muted `#57606a`, accent `#3b82d4` (sparingly), secondary `#7c5cd8` (rarely).

You have access to `spawn_subagent` which creates an independent agent with its own context.

**Default: do the work yourself.** Most tasks are faster and cheaper without a subagent.

- The task is clearly self-contained and only needs a summary back

- You cannot accomplish it with 1-2 direct tool calls

The superseded level works, but the report and the summary line hide it or blur it.
Every item below is the same mistake: a level of evidence that exists in the data
but is conflated or invisible when presented. That is the failure this project was
built to expose, so it cannot ship in its own report.

1. The headline arithmetic does not close. It shows 947 observed (product) with
   938 in-situ and 4 under driver underneath. 938 + 4 is 942. The 5 superseded
   units are inside the 947 but named nowhere. Show superseded as its own figure
   beside the others so the parts sum to the whole, and do the same in the product
   and whole-package scope panels.

2. Reconsider what superseded means for a unit's provenance. Those 5 functions were
   genuinely observed by the test_suite baseline; it is the driver that became
   redundant, not the observation. Right now provenance=superseded replaces
   observed_in_situ, which drops the in-situ count from 943 to 938 and understates
   how much the baselines actually observed. Keep the unit's provenance as
   observed_in_situ and record the redundant driver as an attribute of that unit
   instead. The report should still show these 5 as their own group, described as
   drivers made redundant by a baseline, not as a separate class of observation.

3. The promote-driver summary prints "9/10 promoted, 1 failed" when 4 were promoted,
   5 were superseded and 1 failed. Report the three outcomes separately. A superseded
   driver is not a promotion and counting it as one is the same conflation this tool
   refuses everywhere else.

4. Both baseline cards under "baselines - exactly what was executed" print the same
   command: the full first_light invocation, repeated verbatim in each card. Record
   and show the actual command each runner executed, so the two cards differ. A
   section whose only purpose is to prove what ran cannot show the same string twice.

5. The evidence map legend lists three states and there are now four. Add the missing
   one with its own swatch.

Regenerate evidence.json and report.html. Report the product-scope figures for
never_observed, observed_in_situ, observed_under_driver and superseded, read from
the regenerated file, and confirm they sum to the product total.

2 | """
3 | First Light — which functions have ever been observed executing?
4 | 
5 | Usage:
6 |     python first_light.py --package <pkg_path> --runner <runner.py>
7 |                           [--python <interpreter>]
8 |                           [--exclude <dir> ...]
9 |                           [--rcfile <coverage_rc>]
10 | 
11 | Correctness rule
12 | ----------------
13 | A function is counted as *observed* only when lines inside its **body** were
14 | executed — i.e. lines from node.body[0].lineno onward.  The `def` line itself
15 | always executes at import time, so starting the range at node.lineno would
16 | falsely mark every imported function as observed and inflate the result toward
17 | 100 %.  We therefore start at node.body[0].lineno.
18 | """

20 | from __future__ import annotations
21 | 
22 | import argparse
23 | import ast
24 | import datetime
25 | import hashlib
26 | import json

32 | from pathlib import Path
33 | from typing import NamedTuple

35 | FIRST_LIGHT_VERSION = "0.3.0"
36 | 
37 | # Valid provenance values — the only four that may appear in evidence.json.
38 | # never_observed      : nothing we ran ever entered this function body.
39 | # observed_in_situ    : the system executed it on its own, under normal operation.
40 | # observed_under_driver: it only ran because we built something to reach it.
41 | # superseded          : a driver existed for this unit, but a later baseline also
42 | #                       reached it in situ, making the driver redundant.  The driver
43 | #                       is kept; this provenance records that it is no longer the only
44 | #                       evidence.

46 | PROVENANCE_IN_SITU         = "observed_in_situ"
47 | PROVENANCE_UNDER_DRIVER    = "observed_under_driver"

64 | # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
65 | # Step 1: collect executed lines via coverage.py
66 | # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
67 | 
68 | # Wrapper template injected around the user's runner script.
69 | # It patches os._exit → SystemExit so that any target program that calls
70 | # os._exit() (bypassing atexit handlers) cannot prevent coverage.py from
71 | # flushing its data file.  A warning is printed to stderr when triggered,
72 | # because os._exit() in a target is itself a noteworthy finding.
73 | _WRAPPER_TEMPLATE = '''\
74 | import os as _os
75 | import sys as _sys
76 | 
77 | _real_exit = _os._exit
78 | 
79 | def _patched_exit(code):
80 |     import sys as _s
81 |     print(
82 |         "[first_light] WARNING: target called os._exit(" + str(code) + "); "
83 |         "intercepted to allow coverage flush",
84 |         file=_s.stderr,
85 |         flush=True,
86 |     )
87 |     raise SystemExit(code)
88 | 
89 | _os._exit = _patched_exit
90 | 
91 | try:
92 |     with open({runner_path!r}) as _f:
93 |         _src = _f.read()
94 |     exec(compile(_src, {runner_path!r}, "exec"), {{"__file__": {runner_path!r}, "__name__": "__main__"}})
95 | except SystemExit:
96 |     raise
97 | finally:
98 |     _os._exit = _real_exit
99 | '''
100 | 
101 | 
102 | def collect_coverage(
103 |     package_path: str,
104 |     runner_script: str,
105 |     python: str,
106 |     rcfile: str | None = None,
107 | ) -> tuple[dict[str, set[int]], int, str]:
108 |     """Run *runner_script* under coverage.py and return ({abs_path: {lines}}, exit_code, stdout).
109 | 
110 |     A thin wrapper script is written to a temp file before invoking coverage.
111 |     The wrapper patches os._exit → SystemExit so that targets which call
112 |     os._exit() (like visidata's vd_cli) cannot prevent coverage from writing
113 |     its data file.  A warning is emitted to stderr when the patch fires.
114 | 
115 |     Returns a tuple of (executed_lines_map, runner_exit_code, runner_stdout).
116 |     The exit code is the raw return code of the runner subprocess (after the
117 |     wrapper); it is recorded verbatim in the baseline so the evidence is
118 |     transparent about partial runs (e.g. a test suite where some tests failed
119 |     on this platform).  The stdout is returned so callers can parse runner-
120 |     specific output (e.g. pytest collected/passed/failed counts).
121 |     """
122 |     pkg_abs = str(Path(package_path).resolve())
123 |     runner_abs = str(Path(runner_script).resolve())
124 | 
125 |     with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="first_light_cov_") as tmpdir:
126 |         data_file = os.path.join(tmpdir, ".coverage")
127 | 
128 |         # Write the wrapper that patches os._exit and then exec's the runner.
129 |         wrapper_path = os.path.join(tmpdir, "_fl_wrapper.py")
130 |         with open(wrapper_path, "w") as wf:
131 |             wf.write(_WRAPPER_TEMPLATE.format(runner_path=runner_abs))
132 | 
133 |         cmd = [
134 |             python, "-m", "coverage", "run",
135 |             f"--source={pkg_abs}",
136 |             f"--data-file={data_file}",
137 |             # No --branch flag: line coverage only.
138 |         ]
139 |         if rcfile:
140 |             cmd += [f"--rcfile={rcfile}"]
141 | 
142 |         cmd.append(wrapper_path)
143 | 
144 |         result = subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True)
145 |         runner_exit_code = result.returncode
146 |         runner_stdout = result.stdout or ""
147 |         if result.returncode not in (0, 1):
148 |             # rc 1 is acceptable (e.g. visidata batch mode exits 1 on warnings;
149 |             # pytest exits 1 when tests fail — that is expected on Windows).
150 |             print(f"[first_light] coverage run exited {result.returncode}", file=sys.stderr)
151 |         if result.stderr:
152 |             print(result.stderr[:2000], file=sys.stderr)
153 | 
154 |         # Export to JSON so we don't need to import coverage internals
155 |         json_path = os.path.join(tmpdir, "coverage.json")
156 |         export_cmd = [
157 |             python, "-m", "coverage", "json",
158 |             f"--data-file={data_file}",
159 |             "-o", json_path,
160 |             "--pretty-print",
161 |         ]
162 |         if rcfile:
163 |             export_cmd += [f"--rcfile={rcfile}"]
164 | 
165 |         export_result = subprocess.run(export_cmd, capture_output=True, text=True)
166 |         if export_result.returncode != 0:
167 |             print("[first_light] coverage json export failed:", file=sys.stderr)
168 |             print(export_result.stderr[:2000], file=sys.stderr)
169 |             return {}, runner_exit_code, runner_stdout
170 | 
171 |         with open(json_path) as fh:
172 |             data = json.load(fh)
173 | 
174 |         executed: dict[str, set[int]] = {}
175 |         for file_path, file_data in data.get("files", {}).items():
176 |             abs_path = str(Path(file_path).resolve())
177 |             executed_lines = set(file_data.get("executed_lines", []))
178 |             executed[abs_path] = executed_lines
179 | 
180 |     return executed, runner_exit_code, runner_stdout
181 |

183 | def _parse_pytest_counts(stdout: str) -> tuple[int | None, int | None, int | None]:
184 |     """Parse collected/passed/failed counts from pytest's summary line.
185 | 
186 |     pytest prints a line like:
187 |         "5 passed, 2 failed in 3.14s"
188 |         "7 passed in 1.23s"
189 |         "3 failed in 0.45s"
190 |         "10 passed, 2 warnings in 5.00s"
191 |     (or a '=' separator line when --no-header is used).
192 | 
193 |     Returns (collected, passed, failed) as ints, or (None, None, None) if
194 |     the summary line is not found.
195 |     """
196 |     import re as _re
197 |     passed = failed = collected = None
198 |     for line in reversed(stdout.splitlines()):
199 |         m_passed = _re.search(r'(\d+)\s+passed', line)
200 |         m_failed = _re.search(r'(\d+)\s+failed', line)
201 |         m_error  = _re.search(r'(\d+)\s+error', line)
202 |         if m_passed or m_failed or m_error:
203 |             passed  = int(m_passed.group(1)) if m_passed else 0
204 |             failed  = int(m_failed.group(1)) if m_failed else 0
205 |             if m_error:
206 |                 failed = (failed or 0) + int(m_error.group(1))
207 |             # "collected N items" line appears earlier
208 |             for prev_line in stdout.splitlines():
209 |                 m_coll = _re.search(r'collected\s+(\d+)\s+item', prev_line)
210 |                 if m_coll:
211 |                     collected = int(m_coll.group(1))
212 |                     break
213 |             if collected is None:
214 |                 collected = (passed or 0) + (failed or 0)
215 |             return collected, passed, failed
216 |     return None, None, None

219 | # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
220 | # Step 2: enumerate all functions via ast
221 | # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
222 | 
223 | def iter_functions(source_path: Path, pkg_root: Path) -> list[FuncInfo]:
224 |     """Parse *source_path* and yield FuncInfo for every function definition."""
225 |     try:
226 |         source = source_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
227 |         tree = ast.parse(source, filename=str(source_path))
228 |     except SyntaxError:
229 |         return []
230 | 
231 |     rel = source_path.relative_to(pkg_root.parent)
232 |     # Build a dotted module prefix: visidata/column.py -> visidata.column
233 |     module_parts = list(rel.with_suffix("").parts)
234 |     if module_parts[-1] == "__init__":
235 |         module_parts = module_parts[:-1]
236 |     module_name = ".".join(module_parts)
237 | 
238 |     funcs: list[FuncInfo] = []
239 | 
240 |     def _visit(node: ast.AST, scope: str) -> None:
241 |         for child in ast.iter_child_nodes(node):
242 |             if isinstance(child, (ast.FunctionDef, ast.AsyncFunctionDef)):
243 |                 # Build the qualified name
244 |                 qname = f"{scope}.{child.name}" if scope else child.name
245 |                 # body_start: first statement of the body
246 |                 if child.body:
247 |                     body_start = child.body[0].lineno
248 |                 else:
249 |                     body_start = child.lineno + 1  # degenerate: empty body
250 |                 body_end = child.end_lineno or body_start
251 | 
252 |                 funcs.append(FuncInfo(
253 |                     qualified_name=qname,
254 |                     file=str(source_path.resolve()),
255 |                     def_line=child.lineno,
256 |                     body_start=body_start,
257 |                     body_end=body_end,
258 |                     is_async=isinstance(child, ast.AsyncFunctionDef),
259 |                 ))
260 |                 # recurse into nested functions / methods
261 |                 _visit(child, qname)
262 |             elif isinstance(child, ast.ClassDef):
263 |                 class_scope = f"{scope}.{child.name}" if scope else child.name
264 |                 _visit(child, class_scope)
265 |             else:
266 |                 _visit(child, scope)
267 | 
268 |     _visit(tree, module_name)
269 |     return funcs
270 |

272 | # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
273 | # Step 3: decide observed / never-observed
274 | # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
275 | 
276 | def classify_functions(
277 |     funcs: list[FuncInfo],
278 |     executed: dict[str, set[int]],
279 | ) -> tuple[list[FuncInfo], list[FuncInfo]]:
280 |     """Return (observed, never_observed) lists."""
281 |     observed = []
282 |     never_observed = []
283 | 
284 |     for fn in funcs:
285 |         file_lines = executed.get(fn.file, set())
286 |         # A function is observed if ANY line in [body_start, body_end] was executed.
287 |         if file_lines.intersection(range(fn.body_start, fn.body_end + 1)):
288 |             observed.append(fn)
289 |         else:
290 |             never_observed.append(fn)
291 | 
292 |     return observed, never_observed
293 |

295 | # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
296 | # Step 4: collect source files, with exclusion support
297 | # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
298 | 
299 | ALWAYS_EXCLUDE = {"__pycache__", ".git", ".tox", ".venv", "venv"}
300 | 
301 | def collect_python_files(
302 |     pkg_path: Path,
303 |     exclude_dirs: set[str],
304 | ) -> list[Path]:
305 |     """Recursively collect .py files under *pkg_path*, skipping *exclude_dirs*."""
306 |     all_dirs = ALWAYS_EXCLUDE | exclude_dirs
307 |     files = []
308 |     for py_file in sorted(pkg_path.rglob("*.py")):
309 |         parts = set(py_file.relative_to(pkg_path).parts)
310 |         if parts & all_dirs:
311 |             continue
312 |         files.append(py_file)
313 |     return files

318 | # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
319 | 
320 | def directory_label(file: str, pkg_root: Path) -> str:
321 |     """Return a short display label for the directory containing *file*."""
322 |     rel = Path(file).relative_to(pkg_root)
323 |     parts = rel.parts
324 |     if len(parts) == 1:
325 |         return "(root)"
326 |     return parts[1] if len(parts) == 2 else "/".join(parts[1:-1])

329 | def build_breakdown(
330 |     funcs: list[FuncInfo],
331 |     observed_set: set[int],  # ids of observed FuncInfo objects
332 |     pkg_root: Path,
333 | ) -> dict[str, dict]:
334 |     """Return per-directory stats dict."""
335 |     by_dir: dict[str, dict] = defaultdict(lambda: {"total": 0, "observed": 0, "never": 0})
336 |     for fn in funcs:
337 |         label = directory_label(fn.file, pkg_root)
338 |         by_dir[label]["total"] += 1
339 |         if id(fn) in observed_set:
340 |             by_dir[label]["observed"] += 1
341 |         else:
342 |             by_dir[label]["never"] += 1
343 |     return dict(sorted(by_dir.items()))

350 | def _sha256(path: str) -> str:
351 |     """Return the hex SHA-256 of a file's current contents."""
352 |     h = hashlib.sha256()
353 |     with open(path, "rb") as fh:
354 |         for chunk in iter(lambda: fh.read(65536), b""):
355 |             h.update(chunk)
356 |     return h.hexdigest()

383 | def write_evidence(
384 |     out_path: str,
385 |     pkg_path: Path,
386 |     exclude_dirs: set[str],
387 |     all_funcs: list[FuncInfo],
388 |     baselines: list[BaselineInfo],
389 | ) -> None:
390 |     """Write the evidence.json artifact to *out_path*.
391 | 
392 |     Schema fields (v0.3.0)
393 |     ----------------------
394 |     generated_at        : ISO-8601 UTC timestamp.
395 |     first_light_version : semver string from FIRST_LIGHT_VERSION.
396 |     baselines           : list of baseline objects, each with:
397 |       id                : short identifier string ("cli", "test_suite", …).
398 |       runner            : absolute path to the runner script.
399 |       package           : absolute path to the analysed package.
400 |       command           : full argv list used to produce the data.
401 |       exit_code         : raw exit code of the runner subprocess.
402 |       excluded_dirs     : directory names excluded from the product-code figure.
403 |       pytest_collected  : (optional) number of tests collected, when runner is pytest.
404 |       pytest_passed     : (optional) number of tests that passed.
405 |       pytest_failed     : (optional) number of tests that failed.
406 |     integrity           : per-file SHA-256 of every analysed source file.
407 |                           The top-level ``stale`` boolean is computed on read
408 |                           by fl_hook.py — it is NOT stored here (it's a
409 |                           derived property, not an observation).
410 |     units               : dict keyed by ``module::qualname``.
411 |       file              : absolute path to the source file.
412 |       def_line          : line number of the ``def`` keyword.
413 |       body_start        : first line of the body (node.body[0].lineno).
414 |       body_end          : last line of the body (node.end_lineno).
415 |       provenance        : one of PROVENANCE_* constants.
416 |                           A unit is observed_in_situ when ANY baseline observed
417 |                           it (unless promoted to observed_under_driver).
418 |                           A unit is superseded when it was previously
419 |                           observed_under_driver but a baseline now also
420 |                           reaches it in situ.
421 |       observed_in_baseline : list of baseline ids that observed this unit.
422 |                           An empty list means never_observed.
423 |     """
424 |     now = datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc).isoformat()
425 | 
426 |     # ── integrity: hash every source file that was analysed ──────────────
427 |     seen_files: set[str] = {fn.file for fn in all_funcs}
428 |     integrity: dict[str, str] = {}
429 |     for fpath in sorted(seen_files):
430 |         try:
431 |             integrity[fpath] = _sha256(fpath)
432 |         except OSError:
433 |             integrity[fpath] = ""
434 | 
435 |     # ── per-baseline observed-id sets ────────────────────────────────────
436 |     # For each baseline, compute which FuncInfo ids were observed.
437 |     baseline_obs: dict[str, set[int]] = {}
438 |     for bl in baselines:
439 |         obs, _ = classify_functions(all_funcs, bl.executed)
440 |         baseline_obs[bl.id] = {id(fn) for fn in obs}
441 | 
442 |     # ── units: one entry per function ────────────────────────────────────
443 |     units: dict[str, dict] = {}
444 |     for fn in all_funcs:
445 |         key = f"{fn.file}::{fn.qualified_name}#{fn.def_line}"
446 |         if key in units:
447 |             print(
448 |                 f"[first_light] WARNING: unit key collision on {key!r} — "
449 |                 f"two functions share the same file, qualified name, and def_line. "
450 |                 f"One entry will be overwritten. This is a bug in the analyser.",
451 |                 file=sys.stderr,
452 |             )
453 |         fn_id = id(fn)
454 |         observed_in = [bl.id for bl in baselines if fn_id in baseline_obs[bl.id]]
455 |         provenance = PROVENANCE_IN_SITU if observed_in else PROVENANCE_NEVER
456 |         units[key] = {
457 |             "file": fn.file,
458 |             "def_line": fn.def_line,
459 |             "body_start": fn.body_start,
460 |             "body_end": fn.body_end,
461 |             "provenance": provenance,
462 |             "observed_in_baseline": observed_in,
463 |         }
464 | 
465 |     # ── baselines list ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
466 |     pkg_abs = str(pkg_path.resolve())
467 |     baselines_doc = []
468 |     for bl in baselines:
469 |         entry: dict = {
470 |             "id": bl.id,
471 |             "runner": str(Path(bl.runner_script).resolve()),
472 |             "package": pkg_abs,
473 |             "command": bl.cmd,
474 |             "exit_code": bl.exit_code,
475 |             "excluded_dirs": sorted(exclude_dirs),
476 |         }
477 |         if bl.pytest_collected is not None:
478 |             entry["pytest_collected"] = bl.pytest_collected
479 |         if bl.pytest_passed is not None:
480 |             entry["pytest_passed"] = bl.pytest_passed
481 |         if bl.pytest_failed is not None:
482 |             entry["pytest_failed"] = bl.pytest_failed
483 |         baselines_doc.append(entry)
484 | 
485 |     doc = {
486 |         "generated_at": now,
487 |         "first_light_version": FIRST_LIGHT_VERSION,
488 |         "baselines": baselines_doc,
489 |         "integrity": integrity,
490 |         "units": units,
491 |     }
492 | 
493 |     with open(out_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
494 |         json.dump(doc, fh, indent=2)

501 | def _driver_call_site(driver_path: Path) -> tuple[str, bool]:
502 |     """Extract the call site declaration from a driver file.
503 | 
504 |     Returns (call_site_text, is_indirect) where:
505 |       call_site_text : the text following "call site:" or "call site (indirect):",
506 |                        or '' if no such comment exists.
507 |       is_indirect    : True when the comment begins with "call site (indirect):".
508 | 
509 |     Indirect call site format (two semicolon-separated parts):
510 |         # call site (indirect): file:N -- dispatch_code ; file:M -- binding_name
511 | 
512 |     Direct call site format (single part, unchanged):
513 |         # call site: file:N -- funcname(...)
514 |     """
515 |     try:
516 |         text = driver_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
517 |         for line in text.splitlines():
518 |             stripped = line.strip().lstrip("#").strip()
519 |             lower = stripped.lower()
520 |             if lower.startswith("call site (indirect):"):
521 |                 return stripped[len("call site (indirect):"):].strip(), True
522 |             if lower.startswith("call site:"):
523 |                 return stripped[len("call site:"):].strip(), False
524 |         # Fallback: look for 'Real call site' / 'call site' in docstring lines
525 |         for line in text.splitlines():
526 |             lower_line = line.lower()
527 |             if "call site" in lower_line and "--" in line:
528 |                 after = line[line.index("--"):].strip(" -")
529 |                 if after:
530 |                     return after, False
531 |     except OSError:
532 |         pass
533 |     return "", False

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
First Light — which functions have ever been observed executing?

Usage:
    python first_light.py --package <pkg_path> --runner <runner.py>
                          [--python <interpreter>]
                          [--exclude <dir> ...]
                          [--rcfile <coverage_rc>]

Correctness rule
----------------
A function is counted as *observed* only when lines inside its **body** were
executed — i.e. lines from node.body[0].lineno onward.  The `def` line itself
always executes at import time, so starting the range at node.lineno would
falsely mark every imported function as observed and inflate the result toward
100 %.  We therefore start at node.body[0].lineno.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import ast
import datetime
import hashlib
import json
import os
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
from collections import defaultdict
from pathlib import Path
from typing import NamedTuple

FIRST_LIGHT_VERSION = "0.3.0"

# Valid provenance values — the only four that may appear in evidence.json.
# never_observed      : nothing we ran ever entered this function body.
# observed_in_situ    : the system executed it on its own, under normal operation.
# observed_under_driver: it only ran because we built something to reach it.
# superseded          : a driver existed for this unit, but a later baseline also
#                       reached it in situ, making the driver redundant.  The driver
#                       is kept; this provenance records that it is no longer the only
#                       evidence.
PROVENANCE_NEVER           = "never_observed"
PROVENANCE_IN_SITU         = "observed_in_situ"
PROVENANCE_UNDER_DRIVER    = "observed_under_driver"
PROVENANCE_SUPERSEDED      = "superseded"


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Data model
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

class FuncInfo(NamedTuple):
    qualified_name: str   # e.g. "visidata.column.Column.getValue"
    file: str             # absolute path
    def_line: int         # line of the `def` keyword
    body_start: int       # first line of the body (node.body[0].lineno)
    body_end: int         # last line of the body (node.end_lineno)
    is_async: bool


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Step 1: collect executed lines via coverage.py
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Wrapper template injected around the user's runner script.
# It patches os._exit → SystemExit so that any target program that calls
# os._exit() (bypassing atexit handlers) cannot prevent coverage.py from
# flushing its data file.  A warning is printed to stderr when triggered,
# because os._exit() in a target is itself a noteworthy finding.
_WRAPPER_TEMPLATE = '''\
import os as _os
import sys as _sys

_real_exit = _os._exit

def _patched_exit(code):
    import sys as _s
    print(
        "[first_light] WARNING: target called os._exit(" + str(code) + "); "
        "intercepted to allow coverage flush",
        file=_s.stderr,
        flush=True,
    )
    raise SystemExit(code)

_os._exit = _patched_exit

try:
    with open({runner_path!r}) as _f:
        _src = _f.read()
    exec(compile(_src, {runner_path!r}, "exec"), {{"__file__": {runner_path!r}, "__name__": "__main__"}})
except SystemExit:
    raise
finally:
    _os._exit = _real_exit
'''


def collect_coverage(
    package_path: str,
    runner_script: str,
    python: str,
    rcfile: str | None = None,
) -> tuple[dict[str, set[int]], int, str]:
    """Run *runner_script* under coverage.py and return ({abs_path: {lines}}, exit_code, stdout).

    A thin wrapper script is written to a temp file before invoking coverage.
    The wrapper patches os._exit → SystemExit so that targets which call
    os._exit() (like visidata's vd_cli) cannot prevent coverage from writing
    its data file.  A warning is emitted to stderr when the patch fires.

    Returns a tuple of (executed_lines_map, runner_exit_code, runner_stdout).
    The exit code is the raw return code of the runner subprocess (after the
    wrapper); it is recorded verbatim in the baseline so the evidence is
    transparent about partial runs (e.g. a test suite where some tests failed
    on this platform).  The stdout is returned so callers can parse runner-
    specific output (e.g. pytest collected/passed/failed counts).
    """
    pkg_abs = str(Path(package_path).resolve())
    runner_abs = str(Path(runner_script).resolve())

    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="first_light_cov_") as tmpdir:
        data_file = os.path.join(tmpdir, ".coverage")

        # Write the wrapper that patches os._exit and then exec's the runner.
        wrapper_path = os.path.join(tmpdir, "_fl_wrapper.py")
        with open(wrapper_path, "w") as wf:
            wf.write(_WRAPPER_TEMPLATE.format(runner_path=runner_abs))

        cmd = [
            python, "-m", "coverage", "run",
            f"--source={pkg_abs}",
            f"--data-file={data_file}",
            # No --branch flag: line coverage only.
        ]
        if rcfile:
            cmd += [f"--rcfile={rcfile}"]

        cmd.append(wrapper_path)

        result = subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True)
        runner_exit_code = result.returncode
        runner_stdout = result.stdout or ""
        if result.returncode not in (0, 1):
            # rc 1 is acceptable (e.g. visidata batch mode exits 1 on warnings;
            # pytest exits 1 when tests fail — that is expected on Windows).
            print(f"[first_light] coverage run exited {result.returncode}", file=sys.stderr)
        if result.stderr:
            print(result.stderr[:2000], file=sys.stderr)

        # Export to JSON so we don't need to import coverage internals
        json_path = os.path.join(tmpdir, "coverage.json")
        export_cmd = [
            python, "-m", "coverage", "json",
            f"--data-file={data_file}",
            "-o", json_path,
            "--pretty-print",
        ]
        if rcfile:
            export_cmd += [f"--rcfile={rcfile}"]

        export_result = subprocess.run(export_cmd, capture_output=True, text=True)
        if export_result.returncode != 0:
            print("[first_light] coverage json export failed:", file=sys.stderr)
            print(export_result.stderr[:2000], file=sys.stderr)
            return {}, runner_exit_code, runner_stdout

        with open(json_path) as fh:
            data = json.load(fh)

        executed: dict[str, set[int]] = {}
        for file_path, file_data in data.get("files", {}).items():
            abs_path = str(Path(file_path).resolve())
            executed_lines = set(file_data.get("executed_lines", []))
            executed[abs_path] = executed_lines

    return executed, runner_exit_code, runner_stdout


def _parse_pytest_counts(stdout: str) -> tuple[int | None, int | None, int | None]:
    """Parse collected/passed/failed counts from pytest's summary line.

    pytest prints a line like:
        "5 passed, 2 failed in 3.14s"
        "7 passed in 1.23s"
        "3 failed in 0.45s"
        "10 passed, 2 warnings in 5.00s"
    (or a '=' separator line when --no-header is used).

    Returns (collected, passed, failed) as ints, or (None, None, None) if
    the summary line is not found.
    """
    import re as _re
    passed = failed = collected = None
    for line in reversed(stdout.splitlines()):
        m_passed = _re.search(r'(\d+)\s+passed', line)
        m_failed = _re.search(r'(\d+)\s+failed', line)
        m_error  = _re.search(r'(\d+)\s+error', line)
        if m_passed or m_failed or m_error:
            passed  = int(m_passed.group(1)) if m_passed else 0
            failed  = int(m_failed.group(1)) if m_failed else 0
            if m_error:
                failed = (failed or 0) + int(m_error.group(1))
            # "collected N items" line appears earlier
            for prev_line in stdout.splitlines():
                m_coll = _re.search(r'collected\s+(\d+)\s+item', prev_line)
                if m_coll:
                    collected = int(m_coll.group(1))
                    break
            if collected is None:
                collected = (passed or 0) + (failed or 0)
            return collected, passed, failed
    return None, None, None


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Step 2: enumerate all functions via ast
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def iter_functions(source_path: Path, pkg_root: Path) -> list[FuncInfo]:
    """Parse *source_path* and yield FuncInfo for every function definition."""
    try:
        source = source_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
        tree = ast.parse(source, filename=str(source_path))
    except SyntaxError:
        return []

    rel = source_path.relative_to(pkg_root.parent)
    # Build a dotted module prefix: visidata/column.py -> visidata.column
    module_parts = list(rel.with_suffix("").parts)
    if module_parts[-1] == "__init__":
        module_parts = module_parts[:-1]
    module_name = ".".join(module_parts)

    funcs: list[FuncInfo] = []

    def _visit(node: ast.AST, scope: str) -> None:
        for child in ast.iter_child_nodes(node):
            if isinstance(child, (ast.FunctionDef, ast.AsyncFunctionDef)):
                # Build the qualified name
                qname = f"{scope}.{child.name}" if scope else child.name
                # body_start: first statement of the body
                if child.body:
                    body_start = child.body[0].lineno
                else:
                    body_start = child.lineno + 1  # degenerate: empty body
                body_end = child.end_lineno or body_start

                funcs.append(FuncInfo(
                    qualified_name=qname,
                    file=str(source_path.resolve()),
                    def_line=child.lineno,
                    body_start=body_start,
                    body_end=body_end,
                    is_async=isinstance(child, ast.AsyncFunctionDef),
                ))
                # recurse into nested functions / methods
                _visit(child, qname)
            elif isinstance(child, ast.ClassDef):
                class_scope = f"{scope}.{child.name}" if scope else child.name
                _visit(child, class_scope)
            else:
                _visit(child, scope)

    _visit(tree, module_name)
    return funcs


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Step 3: decide observed / never-observed
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def classify_functions(
    funcs: list[FuncInfo],
    executed: dict[str, set[int]],
) -> tuple[list[FuncInfo], list[FuncInfo]]:
    """Return (observed, never_observed) lists."""
    observed = []
    never_observed = []

    for fn in funcs:
        file_lines = executed.get(fn.file, set())
        # A function is observed if ANY line in [body_start, body_end] was executed.
        if file_lines.intersection(range(fn.body_start, fn.body_end + 1)):
            observed.append(fn)
        else:
            never_observed.append(fn)

    return observed, never_observed


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Step 4: collect source files, with exclusion support
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

ALWAYS_EXCLUDE = {"__pycache__", ".git", ".tox", ".venv", "venv"}

def collect_python_files(
    pkg_path: Path,
    exclude_dirs: set[str],
) -> list[Path]:
    """Recursively collect .py files under *pkg_path*, skipping *exclude_dirs*."""
    all_dirs = ALWAYS_EXCLUDE | exclude_dirs
    files = []
    for py_file in sorted(pkg_path.rglob("*.py")):
        parts = set(py_file.relative_to(pkg_path).parts)
        if parts & all_dirs:
            continue
        files.append(py_file)
    return files


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Step 5: build per-directory breakdown
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def directory_label(file: str, pkg_root: Path) -> str:
    """Return a short display label for the directory containing *file*."""
    rel = Path(file).relative_to(pkg_root)
    parts = rel.parts
    if len(parts) == 1:
        return "(root)"
    return parts[1] if len(parts) == 2 else "/".join(parts[1:-1])


def build_breakdown(
    funcs: list[FuncInfo],
    observed_set: set[int],  # ids of observed FuncInfo objects
    pkg_root: Path,
) -> dict[str, dict]:
    """Return per-directory stats dict."""
    by_dir: dict[str, dict] = defaultdict(lambda: {"total": 0, "observed": 0, "never": 0})
    for fn in funcs:
        label = directory_label(fn.file, pkg_root)
        by_dir[label]["total"] += 1
        if id(fn) in observed_set:
            by_dir[label]["observed"] += 1
        else:
            by_dir[label]["never"] += 1
    return dict(sorted(by_dir.items()))

# evidence.json writer
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def _sha256(path: str) -> str:
    """Return the hex SHA-256 of a file's current contents."""
    h = hashlib.sha256()
    with open(path, "rb") as fh:
        for chunk in iter(lambda: fh.read(65536), b""):
            h.update(chunk)
    return h.hexdigest()


class BaselineInfo:
    """All the metadata and coverage results for one baseline run."""
    def __init__(
        self,
        baseline_id: str,
        runner_script: str,
        cmd: list[str],
        exit_code: int,
        executed: dict[str, set[int]],
        pytest_collected: int | None = None,
        pytest_passed: int | None = None,
        pytest_failed: int | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        self.id = baseline_id
        self.runner_script = runner_script
        self.cmd = cmd
        self.exit_code = exit_code
        self.executed = executed  # {abs_path: {executed_line_numbers}}
        # Optional pytest counts (None when the runner is not pytest)
        self.pytest_collected = pytest_collected
        self.pytest_passed = pytest_passed
        self.pytest_failed = pytest_failed


def write_evidence(
    out_path: str,
    pkg_path: Path,
    exclude_dirs: set[str],
    all_funcs: list[FuncInfo],
    baselines: list[BaselineInfo],
) -> None:
    """Write the evidence.json artifact to *out_path*.

    Schema fields (v0.3.0)
    ----------------------
    generated_at        : ISO-8601 UTC timestamp.
    first_light_version : semver string from FIRST_LIGHT_VERSION.
    baselines           : list of baseline objects, each with:
      id                : short identifier string ("cli", "test_suite", …).
      runner            : absolute path to the runner script.
      package           : absolute path to the analysed package.
      command           : full argv list used to produce the data.
      exit_code         : raw exit code of the runner subprocess.
      excluded_dirs     : directory names excluded from the product-code figure.
      pytest_collected  : (optional) number of tests collected, when runner is pytest.
      pytest_passed     : (optional) number of tests that passed.
      pytest_failed     : (optional) number of tests that failed.
    integrity           : per-file SHA-256 of every analysed source file.
                          The top-level ``stale`` boolean is computed on read
                          by fl_hook.py — it is NOT stored here (it's a
                          derived property, not an observation).
    units               : dict keyed by ``module::qualname``.
      file              : absolute path to the source file.
      def_line          : line number of the ``def`` keyword.
      body_start        : first line of the body (node.body[0].lineno).
      body_end          : last line of the body (node.end_lineno).
      provenance        : one of PROVENANCE_* constants.
                          A unit is observed_in_situ when ANY baseline observed
                          it (unless promoted to observed_under_driver).
                          A unit is superseded when it was previously
                          observed_under_driver but a baseline now also
                          reaches it in situ.
      observed_in_baseline : list of baseline ids that observed this unit.
                          An empty list means never_observed.
    """
    now = datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc).isoformat()

    # ── integrity: hash every source file that was analysed ──────────────
    seen_files: set[str] = {fn.file for fn in all_funcs}
    integrity: dict[str, str] = {}
    for fpath in sorted(seen_files):
        try:
            integrity[fpath] = _sha256(fpath)
        except OSError:
            integrity[fpath] = ""

    # ── per-baseline observed-id sets ────────────────────────────────────
    # For each baseline, compute which FuncInfo ids were observed.
    baseline_obs: dict[str, set[int]] = {}
    for bl in baselines:
        obs, _ = classify_functions(all_funcs, bl.executed)
        baseline_obs[bl.id] = {id(fn) for fn in obs}

    # ── units: one entry per function ────────────────────────────────────
    units: dict[str, dict] = {}
    for fn in all_funcs:
        key = f"{fn.file}::{fn.qualified_name}#{fn.def_line}"
        if key in units:
            print(
                f"[first_light] WARNING: unit key collision on {key!r} — "
                f"two functions share the same file, qualified name, and def_line. "
                f"One entry will be overwritten. This is a bug in the analyser.",
                file=sys.stderr,
            )
        fn_id = id(fn)
        observed_in = [bl.id for bl in baselines if fn_id in baseline_obs[bl.id]]
        provenance = PROVENANCE_IN_SITU if observed_in else PROVENANCE_NEVER
        units[key] = {
            "file": fn.file,
            "def_line": fn.def_line,
            "body_start": fn.body_start,
            "body_end": fn.body_end,
            "provenance": provenance,
            "observed_in_baseline": observed_in,
        }

    # ── baselines list ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    pkg_abs = str(pkg_path.resolve())
    baselines_doc = []
    for bl in baselines:
        entry: dict = {
            "id": bl.id,
            "runner": str(Path(bl.runner_script).resolve()),
            "package": pkg_abs,
            "command": bl.cmd,
            "exit_code": bl.exit_code,
            "excluded_dirs": sorted(exclude_dirs),
        }
        if bl.pytest_collected is not None:
            entry["pytest_collected"] = bl.pytest_collected
        if bl.pytest_passed is not None:
            entry["pytest_passed"] = bl.pytest_passed
        if bl.pytest_failed is not None:
            entry["pytest_failed"] = bl.pytest_failed
        baselines_doc.append(entry)

    doc = {
        "generated_at": now,
        "first_light_version": FIRST_LIGHT_VERSION,
        "baselines": baselines_doc,
        "integrity": integrity,
        "units": units,
    }

    with open(out_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        json.dump(doc, fh, indent=2)

def _driver_call_site(driver_path: Path) -> tuple[str, bool]:
    """Extract the call site declaration from a driver file.

    Returns (call_site_text, is_indirect) where:
      call_site_text : the text following "call site:" or "call site (indirect):",
                       or '' if no such comment exists.
      is_indirect    : True when the comment begins with "call site (indirect):".

    Indirect call site format (two semicolon-separated parts):
        # call site (indirect): file:N -- dispatch_code ; file:M -- binding_name

    Direct call site format (single part, unchanged):
        # call site: file:N -- funcname(...)
    """
    try:
        text = driver_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
        for line in text.splitlines():
            stripped = line.strip().lstrip("#").strip()
            lower = stripped.lower()
            if lower.startswith("call site (indirect):"):
                return stripped[len("call site (indirect):"):].strip(), True
            if lower.startswith("call site:"):
                return stripped[len("call site:"):].strip(), False
        # Fallback: look for 'Real call site' / 'call site' in docstring lines
        for line in text.splitlines():
            lower_line = line.lower()
            if "call site" in lower_line and "--" in line:
                after = line[line.index("--"):].strip(" -")
                if after:
                    return after, False
    except OSError:
        pass
    return "", False
